The bounded deductions needed below are independently reconstructed as follows. Complete smooth gradients against any positive closed T. Uniformly zero functions have zero strong-gradient limit by testing closedness against compact smooth forms and finite coefficient measures. For uniformly convergent bounded psh fj, |fj|<=A, nested cutoffs chi,eta and epsilon=||fj-fk|| give Q_(T,chi)(fj-fk)<=epsilon^2||DDchi T||TV/2+2A epsilon||chi||infinity||DDeta T||TV. On a common nonpositive energy sublevel>=-C, tangent dual and midpoint domination give int(-a)MA(b)<=3C, int(-a)B(b,w)<=6C and Q_theta_w(a)<=6C. With f=a-b, g=(a+b)/2,h=w-g, transgression expresses Q_theta_w(f)-I/2 as the difference of two endpoint pairings. Each h-gradient has bound12C+3C+6C=21C; Cauchy--Schwarz gives Q_theta_w(f)<=I/2+sqrt(42CI). Fixed finite coordinate paths, actual curve fibre caps and Cauchy--Schwarz control Gauss-grid oscillation; first fix a grid and let I->0, then refine it. Every full point has independent homogeneous Laurent Abhyankar coordinates. CLD11.6.3/5(c),13.8.1--5 give a finite-flat singleton Gauss representative. Thus the fixed-test modulus forces a(x)-b(x)->0 as I->0. These full points are dense via Shilov points of small pure affinoid neighborhoods. Actual Laurent caps separate arbitrary points; span(C) is a vector lattice, since max(A(p-q),A(r-s))=2A[max((p+s)/2,(r+q)/2)-(q+s)/2]. Finite maximum/minimum interpolation on compact X proves uniform density in C(X). Green then makes actual bounded MA measures Cauchy on every continuous test as I->0. These facts prove the bounded inputs used below, at the stated conventional foundation boundary.

For clarity, the fast-sequence input is also a deduction. Scaling yields -E(ta)<=t+3t^2(-E(a))/2. Applying a finite full dual to ta bounds normalized maximizing weights in one energy sublevel. Their intersection N is null for every bounded MA measure; positive full-point atoms exclude full points from N. Off O_m, telescoping gives uniform convergence with error<=2^(1-n).
